name: XWF World Heavyweight Championship
notes: Every fact held about this belt comes from one night on another promotion's card: Primetime Central's own New Era of 20 April 2003. The fed's own championship pages were never captured.
epitaph: The belt left the federation to be defended. Primetime Central put it on its own New Era supercard on 20 April 2003 and gave it a no-disqualification match, and what followed was six men on one: the champion, C.R., was jumped before the bell, put through a table by the number one contender, dragged upright by the tag team champions and set up for a splash from the top rope. He moved, and pinned the challenger. The announce desk was still promising an XWF programme that would settle it when the broadcast handed off to the next match. Nothing held names an earlier champion, and nothing held says what happened to the belt afterwards.

name: XWF Tag Team Championship
notes: Attested once, from another promotion's announce desk: at New Era the commentary calls the Monte Brisas Outlaws "the tag team champions" while reporting that C.R. had just laid them out backstage.
epitaph: One line of commentary on an interfed supercard is the whole of what survives of this championship. The Monte Brisas Outlaws held it in April 2003, and the sentence that says so is a sentence about them lying unconscious in their own dressing room. No title change, no earlier holder and no defence of it was ever captured.
